source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Engine - Engine Tune Up, p.6-8

procedures.title: Ignition timing: check and adjust
steps: Start the engine and run it at the idle speed in the tune up chart.
Point the timing light at the timing tab.
Loosen the distributor clamp, turn the distributor body to set timing, then tighten the clamp.
Stop the engine, remove the timing light and reconnect the spark advance hose.
notes: Tab marks are 2° apart; "0" is TDC of No. 1 cylinder and all BTDC settings are on the "A" (advance) side, which has the most marks.

procedures.title: Idle speed and mixture: adjust
steps: Preliminary setting: turn each mixture screw in lightly until it seats, then back out 3 turns (do not tighten against the seat or damage may result).

With the engine at operating temperature, air cleaner on, pre-heater and choke valves fully open, set the idle speed screw to the specified rpm (automatic in Drive, manual in Neutral) (see figure 14 in the manual).
Turn the mixture screw for the highest steady idle, then reset the idle speed screw to the rpm on the decal.
Turn the mixture screw in until rpm drops 20 (lean roll).
Back the mixture screw out 1/4 turn.
Repeat the last 2 steps for the second mixture screw if there is one.
Reset the speed screw to the specified idle if needed.
notes: With air conditioning, set idle with A/C OFF, except 325 hp and 350 hp 327 engines with manual transmission (and L-4/L-6 automatics), which are set with A/C ON.

procedures.title: Crankcase ventilation valve: test
steps: Hook up the tachometer and vacuum gauge as for idle adjustment.
Set the parking brake, start the engine and set idle speed and mixture.
Disconnect the ventilation hose at the valve, block the valve opening and note the rpm change (see figure 15 in the manual).
If rpm changes less than 50, the valve is plugged; replace it.

procedures.title: Cylinder balance test
steps: Connect the tachometer and vacuum gauge.
Start the engine and hold 1500 rpm.
Ground the large clip of the grounding leads and attach the individual leads to every plug except the pair under test (see figure 16 in the manual).
Pair the cylinders by splitting the firing order in half and stacking the halves; V8 firing order 1-8-4-3-6-5-7-2 gives pairs 1-6, 8-5, 4-7, 3-2.
Run the engine on each pair in turn, noting rpm and manifold vacuum.
More than 1 inch of vacuum or 40 rpm difference between pairs means the cylinders are out of balance.
notes: This finds weak cylinders a compression test misses, such as a leaking intake manifold, a valve not opening because of a worn cam, or a bad plug.

procedures.title: Battery: additional test
steps: Test with special battery test equipment to its maker's specifications; see Section 6Y.

procedures.title: Ignition: additional checks
steps: Using suitable test equipment per its maker's instructions, check cranking voltage, ignition switch, distributor resistance, secondary resistance, and ignition output and secondary leakage.

procedures.title: Cranking voltage: test
steps: Disconnect the coil primary lead at the coil negative terminal so the engine will not fire (see figure 17 in the manual).
Connect a voltmeter from the coil primary terminal (resistance wire side) to ground.
Crank the engine with the starter.
